17.0.s.en: (1) The punishment for the worship of idols

17.0.0.en: In the following verses he speaks about the punishment for the worship of idols. And in this verse he directs them to offer sound worship to God by sacrificing an animal without blemish, out of respect and love for God, and because it is a type of Christ, the Lamb without blemish.

17.1.0.en: Transgresseth his covenant: betrays God's covenant.

17.1.1.en: The host of heaven: the planets and the stars.

17.1.2.en: If anyone of God's people dares to betray Him by worshiping idols, whether the planets or the stars or any strange gods, he deserves a great punishment.

17.2.0.en: God stresses the necessity of examining the one who has turned away from His worship to the worship of idols and of making certain of this deed.

17.3.0.en: If the conviction is established, the Lord specifies the sentence that must be applied to the apostate, whether a man or a woman, which is death by stoning. This sentence is carried out at the gates of the city so that it is in the sight of all, and the others see it and take warning.

17.4.0.en: The Lord stresses the necessity of not being hasty, so that the sentence may not be unjust. And He requires that it be supported by the testimony of witnesses, two or at least three, to avoid any doubt about the soundness of the sentence that is issued. The testimony of one witness is not enough to make sure that the accusation is true, and so that there may be no suspicion of bias by one person against another, resorting to spite against him by fabricating this accusation.

17.5.0.en: The witnesses begin by stoning the one who worshiped idols, because they are responsible for their testimony, for if he is innocent they bear his guilt before God. Then the rest of the people stone him after them until he dies, and so they put away evil from the midst of the people.

17.5.1.en: Although God is longsuffering toward us now, our worship of other gods besides Him, such as money, pride and the lusts of the world, deserves death. If we fall, we must repent quickly and strive to return from this apostasy to the worship of God and love for Him.

17.6.s.en: (2) Consulting the priest and the judge

17.6.0.en: Between blood and blood: a murder case between the one killed and the killer.

17.6.1.en: Between plea and plea: a dispute between two parties.

17.6.2.en: Between stroke and stroke: between the one wronged and the aggressor, who could wound himself to appear to be the one wronged.

17.6.3.en: If it is difficult for the local judges in one of the cities of the people of Canaan to decide in some disputes, the problem is referred to a higher judicial body in the large cities. There was a judicial body in the villages and small towns made up of three judges, while in the large cities it was made up of twenty-three judges, and if the matter was too difficult for this higher judicial body it was referred to the highest judicial body, the Sanhedrin, made up of the priests and judges in the city where the house of the Lord is. In all cases the party with the problem is bound to obey the judicial rulings that are issued according to God's Law.

17.7.0.en: Whoever violates the judicial rulings is considered a rebel against God and His Law and must be put to death, and then all the people fear and submit to God's Law and judgment.

17.7.1.en: Christ calls us to resort to the priests to resolve problems (Mt 18:17), and likewise St. Paul the Apostle (1 Cor 6:2). May we consult our fathers the priests and their assistants among the wise servants to solve our problems from their beginning, so that we live in peace and do not need to resort to the courts and all the disturbances they cause.

17.8.0.en: After the people settle in the land of Canaan, they may think of setting up a king for themselves like the rest of the peoples around them and as they saw in Egypt. Although this matter angers God because He is their King, His love for them and His longsuffering led Him to give them conditions for setting up this king, which are:

17.8.1.en: 1- That they pray that God would guide them to the suitable king.

17.8.2.en: 2- That he not be a foreigner, lest he lead them to the worship of idols.

17.9.0.en: He completes the conditions for choosing the king, saying:

17.9.1.en: 3- That he not multiply horses, which were reckoned the greatest military force at that time, lest he become proud and depend on his own strength and not on God, and lest he enter needlessly into wars with those around him, all of which is a burden on his people and at the expense of their material needs and their comfort.

17.9.2.en: 4- That he not resort to Egypt, which was the first empire in the world and the dominant one at that time and remained strong even after the rise of empires after it, in order to acquire more horses from it or to ally himself with it, and so not trust in God, and perhaps become tied to the worship of idols.

17.9.3.en: 5- That he not be preoccupied with his lusts, marrying many women who distract him from God and from leading the people, and who may turn his heart to the worship of idols if they are foreigners, as happened with King Solomon (1 Kgs 11:

17.9.4.en: 6- That he not be preoccupied with wealth, acquiring silver and gold, which would distract him from God and burden his people and make them poor, so that he falls into greed and pride.

17.10.0.en: The seventh condition is that the king write for himself a copy of the Law that the priests have, to read in it always and lead the people according to it, and carry it out, so that he protects himself from pride and prolongs his days in the kingdom, and the people love to have his sons succeed him because they are from him. Godly kings appeared who cared for God's Law and submitted to it, such as David, Hezekiah and Josiah (1 Kgs 11:13, 1 Kgs 16:20, 1 Kgs 21, 22).

17.10.1.en: May you take care to read the Holy Bible and carry out its commandments every day, and so protect yourself from many sins and enjoy fellowship with God.

17.10.2.en: The share of the priests, keeping away from pagan practices, and the prophets

18.0.s.en: (1) The share of the priests from the sacrifices

18.0.0.en: God stresses that the priests and the whole tribe of Levi do not own land in Canaan but devote themselves to the service of God and eat of God's portion, that is, the sacrifices and offerings presented to the house of the Lord; that is, their share is the Lord's share of the offerings.

18.1.0.en: Here he mentions the share of the priests from the sacrifices that the people offer to God, and it includes these parts:

18.1.1.en: 1- The shoulder: it is the right foreleg, which is called the heave shoulder (Ex 29:27, 28, Lev 7:30-34). It signifies the striving of the priest, his walking in the way of God, and his help and care for the people.

18.1.2.en: 2- The two cheeks: they are part of the head, and it is noticed that they are not mentioned in the books of Exodus and Leviticus, perhaps because of their small value, and it was known that they belonged to the priest's share. They signify the priest's speech and teaching.

18.1.3.en: 3- The maw: it means the intestines, and it also is not mentioned in the books of Exodus and Leviticus for the same reason given for the cheeks. It signifies meeting the priest's material needs.

18.1.4.en: 4- The wave breast: it is mentioned in the books of Exodus and Leviticus and not mentioned here, perhaps because it was well known that it belonged to the priest's share, and it is the most important part of the sacrifice.

18.2.0.en: In addition to the priest's share of the sacrifices, he has also a share in the agricultural crops. He had the firstfruits of the wheat, the grape juice and the oil, and also the wool that is shorn from the sheep.

18.3.0.en: The reason for these privileges granted to the priest is, as stated in (v. 1), that he has no land or livestock like the rest of the people to provide him with such needs; its reason is also what is stated here, that he is consecrated to stand in prayer before the Lord in His holy house to perform the ritual and spiritual services, he and his descendants after him, so his material needs must be provided for.

18.4.0.en: It may happen that some Levites have a genuine desire of the heart to devote themselves to the service of the house of the Lord, outside their turn, and so they leave their cities of residence, which are considered a sojourn for them, because they had no share in the land but their cities were given to them by the rest of the tribes, and they come to the house of the Lord and serve there with the rest of their Levite brethren who are on duty; in this case they are also given a full share of the tithes, offerings and other things, in addition to their right to any other source of income from what they inherited from their fathers.

18.4.1.en: God cares for His consecrated servants and provides for their needs because He is a tender Father who cares for His children, so rely on Him, confident of His love for you, and fear no troubles in the future, for He is with you, ordering your affairs, defending you and protecting you from every evil.

18.5.0.en: Abomination: filth, a vile act and the work of Satan.

18.5.1.en: He warns them, after they dwell in the land of Canaan, not to imitate the pagans around them in their worship of strange gods, for this is rebellion and betrayal of God.

18.6.0.en: He mentions here examples of the forbidden pagan practices, which are:

18.6.1.en: 1- Human sacrifices: He forbids them to offer their children to be burned with fire or to roast them on the bronze heated with fire, which is the image of the god Molech.

18.6.2.en: 2- Divination: claiming to know the unseen, whether by interpreting dreams, the stars or the palm of the hand ...

18.6.3.en: 3- Augury: it means taking omens of good fortune and of ill fortune.

18.6.5.en: 5- Witchcraft: using the power of Satan to carry out a benefit or ward off harm or hurt others by using spells and riddles.

18.6.6.en: 6- One who charms with a charm: presenting requests to the gods with incense.

18.6.7.en: 7- One who asks a jinn or a familiar spirit: these are kinds of demons, and they thought that there are spirits that attend upon human beings, so they ask for their help.

18.6.8.en: 8- One who consults the dead: that is, summoning spirits, which is calling up demons who pretend to be the spirits of the dead.

18.7.0.en: The Lord wants us to depend on Him alone, so everyone who practices these deeds is an abomination to Him, because they mean relying on satanic powers that do not want good for the children of men and draw them toward disobedience against God. Therefore it was one of the reasons for which the Lord drove the Canaanites out of the land.

18.8.0.en: God asks His children, whether in the Old Testament or in the New Testament, to be perfect. And these defiled deeds deprive the believers of the perfection that the Lord commanded them to seek, as in (Gen 17:1), (Mt 5:48), for they lower the dignity of man and his divine image, since he seeks the help of the enemy of humanity, the enemy of good, ignoring Almighty God.

18.9.1.en: It is not strange that the pagan peoples resort to such defiled deeds, for they believe in vanities because of their inability to perceive the existence of the true God, therefore God permits His people to take their place in the land from which He drives them out. But as for them, they are a royal race, a holy nation and a chosen people; these foolish, defiled deeds are not fitting for them and the Lord does not allow them.

18.9.2.en: Do not let your heart be attached to knowing the unseen or be dazzled by the works of demons, even if they hide behind repeating prayers from the Holy Bible, but seek the Lord your God, and He will guide you and deliver you and keep you from these satanic works and solve your problems, so that you do not lower yourself and abase yourself to Satan your enemy.

18.10.s.en: (3) The true and the false prophets

18.10.0.en: After the Lord forbade resorting to magic and the knowledge of the unseen and condemned their practice, He promised His people that He would raise up a series of prophets whom they would ask and listen to, not false prophets but those sent from the Lord. And these prophets the Lord chooses from within their tribes, that is, from the sons of Jacob, and not strangers. And they will be like Moses, that is, with the same spirit of care that Moses showed toward his people, and they will continue his work. This divine promise was fulfilled later more completely in the person of the Lord Jesus Christ, who took the office of prophet (He is priest, king and prophet), as He spoke to the people with the words of eternal life, declaring that He does not speak of Himself but speaks what the Father gives Him (Jn 5:45, 46; Acts 3:21-26; Acts 7:37). So this verse is a prophecy of the Incarnation of Christ, and Moses is a type of Christ, and there is a likeness between them, but within limits, because Christ is God (see the commentary on Heb 3 in Part Five of the Encyclopedia).

18.11.0.en: He reminds them of what they asked when they were at Mount Horeb (Ex 20), when they were afraid of the awesome manifestations that surrounded their seeing the glory of the Lord when He gave them the Ten Commandments. They asked that Moses be a mediator between them and the Lord, so that they would no longer be terrified and lest they die. And the Lord approved their words and answered them.

18.12.0.en: God alone is the One who raises up the prophets and puts His words in their mouths. (And every prophet afterward would say, "Thus saith the LORD.") And the Lord repeats that the prophets will be from the sons of Jacob and not from foreigners.

18.13.0.en: The person who does not listen to the word of the Lord from the mouth of His prophets and act on it, the Lord will call him to account and judge him. For the Lord requires them to obey His words that come from the mouth of His prophets.

18.14.0.en: A new warning against the false prophets who dare to speak against the Lord, saying words that did not come from Him, claiming that they are divine revelation, and likewise the one who calls to false gods, claiming that he is conveying from them, drawing people to worship them. Such a person is put to death because he leads the people astray.

18.15.0.en: The people may be perplexed before the words of the prophets and unable to judge whether they are truthful or false. Therefore the Lord gave a sign by which they can distinguish between the true prophet and the false prophet, which is: if the things that the prophet prophesied actually happen, his prophecy was true and he spoke on behalf of the Lord, but if they do not happen, this means that he is a false prophet who dared against God and claimed prophecy and conveyed from the Lord words He did not say, so he utters thoughts of his own and not from the inspiration of God.

18.15.1.en: Pay attention to God's word that He sends to you through the mouth of those around you, the priests and teachers, to guide you in the way of your life, and do not be led by the word of the world, however dazzling, for it is false and leads you astray, and in this way you keep your life in tranquility and peace.

18.15.2.en: Cities of refuge and false witness

19.0.s.en: (1) Murder and the cities of refuge

19.0.0.en: Cutteth off: destroyed and drove out.

19.0.1.en: God commands them, after the pagans, the original inhabitants of the land, are driven out and they dwell in their place in the land of Canaan, to set apart three cities to which the unintentional killer may flee. Note that Moses had set apart three cities east of the Jordan for refuge, other than these three which he wants to set apart west of the Jordan (Num 35:

19.1.0.en: He must repair and prepare the roads that lead to those cities so that it is easy for the fleeing killer to run and take refuge in them. They must also divide their land, which the Lord gives them as a portion, into three parts, and it was divided lengthwise from south to north, and in the middle of each part a city of refuge, which is matched east of the Jordan by another city of refuge, so that they have six cities of refuge.

19.2.0.en: He mentions here one of the rulings concerning unintentional killing, and gives an example of it: one who struck his neighbor without intending to kill him, and there was no enmity or quarrel between them before (Num 35:

19.3.0.en: And he gives here a second example of the possibility of killing without intent, which is two persons going to the forest to cut trees; while one of them strikes the trunk of a tree with the axe in order to cut it, the iron part of the axe head slips from the wooden handle and flies far away and strikes his companion and kills him. In this case the killer must flee immediately to the nearest of the three cities set apart for this purpose, to escape being taken in revenge.

19.4.0.en: The avenger of blood: the nearest relative of the person killed, who wants to take vengeance for him on the killer.

19.4.1.en: The unintentional killer must flee quickly to the cities of refuge so that the relative of the one killed, who wants to take revenge for him, does not overtake him when his anger is intense at the killing of his relative, and catch up with him before he reaches the city of refuge and kill him, whereas the Law does not allow that, because the killing of his neighbor was not out of spite or enmity or premeditation, but happened by accident and against his will.

19.5.0.en: So that this may happen, that is, so that the relative of the one killed may not overtake the killer, the Lord commanded them to designate the three cities as cities of refuge, and no one is allowed to kill the killer who reaches one of them (map 9).

19.6.0.en: If the land they possess becomes wide, as the Lord God promised their fathers, so as to include all the lands promised to the fathers (and this depends on their keeping the covenant and their walking according to the commandments and judgments of the Law that God gave them), they must designate three other new cities so that the number of cities of refuge may match the width of the land. Thus they would have nine cities of refuge, but they did not keep God's Law completely, so they did not expand except in the days of David and Solomon, and in the days of these two kings they possessed places but there were no Jews in them, so they did not need the other three cities and were content with the first six set apart for refuge.

19.7.0.en: The Lord made clear that the reason for adding three new cities is that the distance of any city of refuge from all the cities of Israel should be suitable for the one taking refuge in it to reach it in a suitable time, that is, within one day, before the one who wants to take vengeance overtakes him, so that the responsibility for shedding innocent blood would fall on the whole people.

19.8.0.en: In the case of intentional killing, that is, where one person hates another and lies in wait for him and kills him, even if he flees to the cities of refuge the elders of his city bring him from there and the relative of the victim kills him, that is, carries out on him God's sentence of death. But in the New Testament revenge is not permitted and the killer is punished according to the criminal law and the priests help him to repent, so he receives forgiveness of his sins, and even if he is executed he has a place in heaven.

19.9.0.en: He warns them against leniency toward the intentional killer, for he must be punished so that the rest of the people may fear because of the gravity of the sin of murder and show their respect for the life of the one killed, that is, his blood that was shed on the ground.

19.9.1.en: God's tenderness makes Him preserve your life even if you are in the wrong. So thank Him and ask Him to cover you and forgive you your sins, and you also be one who seeks excuses for those around you who go wrong.

19.10.0.en: The landmark: the boundary of the land, which was marked by stones or pieces of iron or trees or by ditches.

19.10.1.en: The Lord forbids the owner of the land to try to enlarge the area of the land he owns at the expense of cutting off a part of his neighbor's lands and annexing it to his own lands, for this is considered a usurpation of the rights of others and an assault on private property. The Lord arranged the way in which the land is distributed to the tribes, families and persons, and departing from this arrangement means making light of the Lord's work and is sometimes a cause of the anger of the wronged owner of the land, who rises up and kills the one who usurped his land.

19.10.2.en: Do not wrong another and usurp his rights. And on the other hand, hold fast to your faith and your rites and do not be lax in them or allow anyone to draw you away from them.

19.11.0.en: The Lord always requires them to investigate and examine cases well before issuing sentences of condemnation. In (ch. 17), when He spoke to them about the punishment of one who worships other gods, He specified the necessity of two or at least three witnesses to testify against him. The same warning against haste and lack of care in judgment He repeats here concerning one who commits some offense or sin, for it requires two or three witnesses to decide the sentence of condemnation, as He also mentioned in (Num 35:30).

19.12.0.en: Testifying wrongfully: swerving away from the truth in his testimony.

19.12.1.en: Here is the ruling on violating the ninth commandment, which was mentioned among the Ten Commandments in (Ex 20:16), which is "Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour." If someone bears false witness against another in order to harm him, the matter is decided as will come in the following verses.

19.13.0.en: Here God sets a system so that no one thinks of taking revenge for himself by himself, which would make matters unstable and cause chaos in people's dealings with one another. He set up a judicial system (ch. 17:8-10) made up of the priests and the judges, and made two levels of judgment, a local level and a central level; so if someone accuses another of a false charge, they appear before the judges.

19.14.0.en: The judges must examine the matter well and be careful, lest they issue unjust sentences. So if it becomes clear to them, after examination and investigation, that the witness accused his companion wrongly and that he is lying in what he said against him, then the same sentence is applied to the witness that the charge he brought against his brother would have required and which would have been applied to his brother had it been true; thus he is punished with the same punishment that he wanted to inflict on his neighbor.

19.15.0.en: The purpose of punishing the false witness is that others may fear and keep away from false witness.

19.16.0.en: He warns them against leniency in punishing the false witness. Whoever testifies against another on a charge whose penalty is death is put to death in his place, and if the penalty is the plucking out of an eye, the breaking of a tooth, or the cutting off of a hand or foot, the false witness is punished with the same penalty.

19.16.1.en: What a person does returns upon him. Therefore let us set the Lord and His fear before us at all times, because we shall suffer the result of what we do.
